Revised assessment: The statement is overall hawkish and contractionary. The 75bp hike to a 3.75–4.00% federal funds range, continued balance-sheet runoff ($60B Treasuries, $35B MBS), and higher administered rates (IORB 3.9%, ON RRP 3.8%) signal a restrictive stance aimed at disinflation. Framed by Taylor-rule logic (with inflation well above the 2% goal and a tight labor market), the guidance that “ongoing increases” will be appropriate fits standard policy prescriptions when the inflation gap is large. The new emphasis on “cumulative tightening” and “lags” tempers this slightly, consistent with the literature on long and variable policy lags (e.g., narrative and VAR evidence in Romer and Romer), but it does not change the fundamentally restrictive stance. The continued QT is consistent with term-structure evidence that balance-sheet policy affects term premia and long rates, while the corridor system (IORB/ON RRP) anchors money-market rates as in the modern operating framework. Citing Russia’s war as a supply shock underscores the adverse inflation-output trade-off highlighted in monetary models; the Committee’s stress on independence and inflation risks echoes the literature’s emphasis on credibility for returning inflation to target. Net effect: modestly negative tone, with hawkish policy outweighing the nod to lags.
